candidates.headline: Attention sparsity does not imply or guarantee that a 5% KV cache preserves the same output token.
candidates.claim: The observation that attention matrices are over 95% sparse under a 1%-of-row-max threshold does not imply or guarantee that retaining only 5% of KV entries preserves the same output token at each decoding step.
candidates.paper_fact: only 5% of the KV cache is sufficient for decoding the same output token at each generation step
candidates.premise: A thresholded attention row can be sparse while the small entries below threshold still contribute to softmax normalization and downstream logits; cache sufficiency requires preserving the computation's effect, not just the count of entries above a threshold.
candidates.inference: The reported sparsity and 5% statement are empirical proxies; they do not by themselves guarantee that a 5% cache preserves the same output token for all steps, layers, and selection policies.
candidates.toy_example: Toy example, not a measurement: a 100-entry attention row with 96 entries below 1% of the row max but whose combined mass is 20% of the softmax; dropping them changes normalization.
candidates.conditional_consequence: If omitted entries carry non-negligible aggregate attention mass or interact with later layers, a 5% cache can change outputs even when measured sparsity exceeds 95%.
candidates.critical_link: Sparsity fraction under a threshold -> sufficiency of a 5% KV cache for identical decoding.
necessary_conditions: Omitted attention entries have negligible aggregate effect on softmax and downstream logits
Selection policy identifies output-relevant entries
Sparsity and selection are stable across decoding steps, layers, and heads
Evaluation checks output equivalence or task accuracy under the same budget
defeaters: Formal proof that any 5% selection preserving top attention mass yields identical outputs
Empirical output-equivalence across tasks and models
Evidence omitted mass is negligible in aggregate
do_not_infer: Do not infer that >95% sparsity guarantees 5% cache preserves accuracy
Do not infer that thresholded sparsity equals cache sufficiency
Do not infer that arbitrary 5% selection is safe

quotes.text: only 5% of the KV cache is sufficient for decoding the same output token at each generation step
even when trained densely, the attention matrices of LLMs are over 95% sparse at inference time
we set the threshold as one percent of the maximum value in each row and calculates the corresponding sparsity

author_boundaries: Authors report empirical sparsity and state 5% sufficiency; their formal guarantee is for greedy H2 under submodular assumptions, not for arbitrary 5% selection.
inferred_consequences: A 5% budget may change outputs if omitted attention mass matters.
Sparsity alone is not a formal cache-sufficiency certificate.
candidates.mechanism: A thresholded attention row can be sparse while the small entries below threshold still contribute to softmax normalization and downstream logits; cache sufficiency requires preserving the computation's effect, not just the count of entries above a threshold. The reported sparsity and 5% statement are empirical proxies; they do not by themselves guarantee that a 5% cache preserves the same output token for all steps, layers, and selection policies.

candidates.headline: Accumulated attention scores favoring older tokens conflicts with unbiased recency-sensitive eviction.
candidates.claim: The paper's local accumulated score can bias retention toward least recent tokens; equal effectiveness does not guarantee unbiased selection.
candidates.paper_fact: employing the accumulated attention score to evict KV embeddings can lead to a potential bias favoring the least recent tokens. candidates.headline: Preallocating KV cache does not imply or guarantee net memory savings
candidates.claim: Preallocating KV cache for a fixed budget does not by itself guarantee that the realized memory footprint falls proportionally with the cache budget.
candidates.paper_fact: memory for KV cache is preallocated. We use a circular queue to update the last K entries efficiently.
candidates.premise: Preallocation reserves capacity up front; if the reserved capacity is sized to the maximum budget or is not fully occupied, resident memory can exceed the active KV entries.
candidates.inference: A 20% KV-cache budget may not translate to a 20% net memory reduction unless preallocation is exactly sized and fully used, so the implementation detail alone does not establish proportional memory savings.

candidates.conditional_consequence: If preallocation over-reserves per layer/head or allocator fragmentation is significant, then net memory saving may be less than the nominal budget reduction suggests.
candidates.critical_link: The preallocated size must equal the active budget and allocator overhead must be small for the budget fraction to bound resident memory.
